nodes.label: API Gateway (Express Gateway)
nodes.rationale: Unico punto de entrada: enrutamiento, autenticacion centralizada OAuth y politicas transversales (rate limiting, logging, CORS) configuradas una sola vez.

nodes.label: Cloud Storage / FTP (almacenamiento CSV)
nodes.rationale: Los CSV no se guardan en el filesystem efimero de contenedores; solo se guarda ruta_almacenamiento en BD.

nodes.label: Logging Centralizado EFK (Elasticsearch, Fluentd, Kibana)
nodes.rationale: Logs de contenedores se pierden al reiniciar/escalar; se requiere correlacionar por id de lote/transaccion y cumplir requisito de auditabilidad.

nodes.label: Patron Adapter / Capa Anticorrupcion
nodes.rationale: Aisla protocolos externos (core bancario, SMTP) del resto del sistema.

nodes.label: Comunicacion hibrida REST sincrono + RabbitMQ asincrono
nodes.norm_label: comunicacion hibrida rest sincrono + rabbitmq asincrono
nodes.rationale: REST cuando el usuario espera respuesta inmediata; RabbitMQ cuando no debe bloquearse el flujo principal.

nodes.label: Patron CQRS
nodes.rationale: Historial separa consulta de escritura manteniendo un modelo de lectura poblado por eventos.

nodes.label: Base de datos por microservicio
nodes.rationale: Cada microservicio es dueno de su BD, sin acceso cruzado; referencias entre servicios son ids externos, no FKs.

nodes.label: Flujo de Aprobacion Maker/Checker/Authorizer
nodes.rationale: Ninguna transaccion llega al core bancario sin revision de tres roles distintos; cada paso auditable en PasoAprobacion; rechazo detiene el flujo.

nodes.label: ProyeccionEventoListener
nodes.rationale: Proyeccion CQRS: el historial se construye consumiendo eventos onLoteCargado/onLoteAprobado.

nodes.label: Diagrama de Secuencia: Aprobacion Maker-Checker-Authorizer
nodes.rationale: Separacion de funciones: tres roles distintos aprueban secuencialmente (pendiente_checker -> pendiente_authorizer -> aprobado) antes de publicar LoteAprobado de forma asincrona.

nodes.label: CI Pipeline (ci.yaml)

nodes.label: Job build (matrix build/push 7 images)
nodes.rationale: OIDC Workload Identity Federation, no JSON keys

nodes.label: AnalysisTemplate k6 smoke
nodes.rationale: Thresholds http_req_failed<1%, p95<500ms; checks relaxed to rate>0.99 after abort

nodes.label: App-of-apps root-sa-p9
nodes.rationale: Root Application creates child apps with sync-waves 0/1/2

nodes.label: Argo Rollouts canary 20/50/80
nodes.rationale: Replaces Deployment; auto-rollback on failed analysis

nodes.label: bootstrap.sh (day-zero entry point)
nodes.rationale: Single entry point, zero manual steps, timestamps for RTO

nodes.label: External Secrets + GCP Secret Manager
nodes.rationale: Secrets survive cluster loss without backing up keys

nodes.label: GitOps (pull-based deployment)
nodes.rationale: Repo GitOps as single source of truth; rebuild = cluster + ArgoCD + repo

nodes.label: Repo software-avanzado-gitops
nodes.rationale: Public, no source code nor secrets; only pipeline PRs and ArgoCD reads

nodes.label: GKE cluster sa-p9
nodes.rationale: Zonal Standard, 3x e2-standard-2, pd-standard due to SSD/E2 quota

nodes.label: Kyverno policies (disallow-latest, require-limits, require-non-root)
nodes.rationale: Enforce scoped to sa-p9 to avoid blocking ArgoCD/Velero/Bitnami

nodes.label: SQLite in emptyDir SPOF
nodes.rationale: Data lost on restart; declared as known loss

nodes.label: Terraform GCS remote state backend
nodes.rationale: P9 requirement; native locking

nodes.label: Terraform layers 00-state/10-base/20-cluster/30-platform
nodes.rationale: Persistent vs destroyable layers so buckets survive cluster destroy

nodes.label: Trampa: ArgoCD vs Velero restore order
nodes.norm_label: trampa: argocd vs velero restore order
nodes.rationale: ArgoCD would create empty MySQL PVC before Velero restores

nodes.label: Velero backups (sa-p9-hourly)
nodes.rationale: Portable backups to dedicated GCS bucket, File System Backup (Kopia), ttl 72h

nodes.label: Workload Identity Federation GitHub->GCP
nodes.rationale: CI SA only has artifactregistry.writer; pipeline never touches cluster

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM email encryption
nodes.rationale: Non-deterministic encryption so ciphertext, IV and authTag stored separately

nodes.label: Logical Foreign Keys
nodes.rationale: References by ID instead of SQL FKs across schemas

nodes.label: Order creation flow
nodes.rationale: Synchronous chain; failures leave order pendiente and report error in impresion.mensaje

nodes.label: requireAuth middleware
nodes.rationale: Validates JWT from httpOnly cookie or Bearer header

nodes.label: Client / Anticorruption Layer
nodes.rationale: figurasClient.js and consumirGramosEnMateriales isolate inter-service GraphQL from business logic

nodes.label: API Gateway Pattern
nodes.rationale: Single entry point centralizes JWT validation and routing; clients never hit microservices directly

nodes.label: Database per Service
nodes.rationale: Each microservice owns its DB; cross-service relations are logical FKs by ID

nodes.label: Healthcheck + Dependency Ordering
nodes.rationale: Compose waits for healthchecks to avoid startup race conditions

nodes.label: Hybrid synchronous REST + GraphQL communication
nodes.rationale: REST for CRUD, GraphQL for flexible typed queries and inter-service calls; internal calls bypass gateway to avoid latency and redundant JWT checks

nodes.label: Proxy / Path Rewrite (http-proxy-middleware)
nodes.rationale: Keeps internal routes independent of external ones

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM encryption
nodes.rationale: Authenticated encryption for nombre/correo which must be readable back; format iv:authTag:cipherText.

nodes.label: HTTP-only cookies
nodes.rationale: Prevents JWT theft via XSS; requires CORS credentials on both sides.

nodes.label: JWT stateless authentication
nodes.rationale: Stateless, scales horizontally; cannot be revoked early, mitigated with short TTL + controlled renewal.

nodes.label: Decoupled authentication and authorization
nodes.rationale: Backend validates identity but delegates permission decisions entirely to the auth microservice via HTTP client with retries/backoff instead of assuming access or failing abruptly.

nodes.label: Password uses hash not AES
nodes.rationale: AES is reversible; passwords must never be recoverable even by the system, so bcrypt is used instead.

nodes.label: --force-recreate for .env changes
nodes.rationale: Env vars are injected at container creation, so a plain restart does not pick up .env changes.

nodes.label: Generic invalid-credentials error
nodes.rationale: Login failure message is intentionally generic so it does not reveal whether the email exists.
